candidates.changed_node: numerator anchor $close -> $open, with TS_MIN($low, 21) -> TS_MIN($low, 63) in both legs
candidates.rationale: Weakest component is the numerator anchor: $close is dividend-adjusted while $low/$high are raw, so the ratio drifts with the adjustment factor, and the 21-day trough re-prices its reference every month (IC decays 0.0250 in 2000 to 0.0010 in 2013). Raw $open removes the scale mix and is known at signal time; a 63-day trough holds the reference through a full quarter. The 63-day windows are also required because the parent's 5-node numerator and 9-node guarded denominator would otherwise be copied verbatim from an archive member and hit the subtree gate. Still bounded in [0,1] since $open <= TS_MAX($high,21).

Regime problem (2003 -0.0051, 2013 -0.0013) sits in the $volume argument: volume level is non-stationary across 2000-2013, so the correlation's second leg drifts with market-wide volume growth and its sign is not stable. Correlating the range with $return makes it an asymmetric-volatility signal whose scale is stationary. One leaf edit; also breaks the shared subtree with the archived TS_DELTA($volume,1) twin at rho 0.615 and cuts the alpha101 overlap from 3 nodes. Window 21 stays inside the 63-day cap for $return terms.

candidates.changed_node: price leg window 10 -> 63 in TS_MEAN($high - $low, .) and TS_MEAN($open, .)
candidates.rationale: The 10-day range/price multiplier is the weak node: price geometry under 21 days has no edge on this panel, and at 10 days the ratio is nearly constant cross-sectionally, so the pair collapses toward plain $roe in the flat years (2003 -0.0035, 2009 +0.0009, 2010 +0.0024). A 63-day realized-range-to-price ratio disperses properly and matches the 57-day half-life of the quality leg. The $roe leg is left alone (3 nodes, under the subtree gate); both window edits are inside the price leg.

candidates.changed_node: price leg windows 21 -> 126 in TS_MIN($low, .) and TS_MEAN($high, .)
candidates.rationale: Horizon mismatch is the defect: the fundamental leg has a 43-day half-life while the 21-day price leg decays in 17.6 days, and that fast leg drives the highest turnover in the population (0.134 one-way). Stretching the trough and the price normaliser to 126 days slows the leg to the fundamental's horizon and cuts the rebalancing it does not earn back. Both window edits are needed anyway: the parent's numerator and its guarded denominator are 5-node subtrees that would be copied verbatim from the archive.

The 21-day ceiling is the weak node. In a sustained rebound almost every name sits near its one-month high, so the multiplier saturates near 1 and carries no cross-sectional dispersion; the factor becomes plain $roa exactly in the years quality lags (2003 -0.0088, 2009 +0.0016). A 126-day ceiling keeps the drawdown ratio dispersed through a recovery. One window edit, and the untouched CS_RANK($roa) leg is only 2 nodes so it clears the subtree gate.

candidates.changed_node: $open denominator -> TS_MEAN($open, 126) (with $roa -> $operating_margin to clear the subtree gate)
candidates.rationale: The single-day $open denominator is the weakest node: dividing a 21-day mean high by one day's open gives a multiplier pinned near 1 with almost no dispersion, so the factor is just the fundamental pair and inherits its dead years (2003 -0.0010, 2006 -0.0040). A 126-day mean open turns it into a real six-month trend ratio that disperses. $roa moves to $operating_margin because the parent's fundamental pair is a 5-node subtree that would otherwise be copied verbatim from the archive, and unlevered margin also cuts the 0.789 correlation with the archived accrual/roe pair.

candidates.changed_node: TS_STD($return, 126) -> TS_STD($return, 63) (left leg re-anchored on raw $open with TS_MEAN to clear the subtree gate)
candidates.rationale: TS_STD($return, 126) is the weak leg: a half-year vol estimate is stale by construction against a 19.7-day IC half-life, and the two losing years (2003 -0.0054, 2013 -0.0045) are the low-vol recoveries where a stale vol rank mislabels names; 63 days tracks the regime and is the tested cap for $return windows. The left leg also mixes adjusted $close with raw $high, so $open replaces it, and TS_MAX -> TS_MEAN is needed because the parent's guarded 189-day denominator is a 5-node archive subtree. Coverage stays bound by the unchanged 189-day window, so it holds near 0.904.

candidates.changed_node: TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) -> TS_DELTA($accrual_gap, 63) (level leg field $roe -> $operating_margin to clear the subtree gate)
candidates.rationale: The factor spends two of its three legs on $leverage, level and 63-day change, so the legs largely cancel and only the transient change survives, which is why the IC half-life is 4.2 days and 2000 and 2001 are negative. Replacing the change leg's field with $accrual_gap gives the second leg independent information and keeps the delta partnered with fundamental ranks, where fundamental deltas have screened well. $roe moves to $operating_margin because the parent's level pair is a 5-node subtree already in the archive and the delta leg is 4 nodes, so both legs had to move.

The single node is the problem: a raw volume level is a size proxy that trends upward across the sample, which is why the signal carries the highest turnover here (0.153 one-way, 0.004 of fitness) yet has decayed to zero by 2013 while never halving inside the 63-day grid. The 21-day change is stationary, prices the surge rather than the size, and steps out of the saturated volume-level slot where a plain level rank already sits at 0.717 against the archived dollar-volume mean. CS_RANK contains the fat tail in volume changes.

candidates.changed_node: the bare $roa leaf, hedged by subtracting RANK($leverage)
candidates.rationale: A bare single-field rank carries an uncontrolled credit-cycle exposure: ROA penalises asset-heavy balance sheets implicitly, and the two negative years (2003 -0.0045, 2006 -0.0026) are the credit-expansion years when that implicit bet drives the ranking. Subtracting an explicit leverage rank makes the exposure deliberate and hedged instead of incidental. Subtracting a second cross-sectional rank is also the move that decorrelates from a single-field archived rank, where multiplying by a bounded positive term does not; three node inserts, and no 4-node subtree is shared with the archived CS_RANK($roe) - CS_RANK($leverage).

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.
